title: European democratic resilience is being reframed as a whole-society security problem spanning rights, trust, participation, and technology
source_unit: Council of Europe, Report of the Secretary General 2026: The New Democratic Pact for Europe in Times of Rupture
geography: Council of Europe member states and broader European democratic-security context, with a focus on institutional, civic, social-rights, information, election, and technology resilience

denominator.unit: Council of Europe member states engaged by the Pact process

dedicated_initiatives.unit: Council of Europe entity initiatives mobilised during the first year

contributions.unit: more than 200 contributions from more than 100 contributors

participant_set.value: governments, parliamentarians, local and regional authorities, international partners, civil society, academia, private sector, and citizens

observations.method: Council of Europe account of a multi-actor consultation process launched in 2025 and structured around learning, protection, and innovation for democratic resilience.
observations.uncertainty: Consultation participation and contribution counts measure institutional engagement, not public opinion, representative citizen preferences, policy adoption, or democratic improvement.
observations.subgroup: Member states, public institutions, civil society, experts, private actors, citizens, young people, minorities, and groups with different access to civic space.
observations.counterinterpretation: A broad consultation can surface diverse priorities, but participation may still be uneven and organized actors may be overrepresented relative to less-engaged citizens.

denominator.unit: Council of Europe synthesis of Pact consultation contributions

participation_orientation.value: democratic participation is framed as a whole-of-society effort requiring civic space, democratic and digital citizenship education, and forms of engagement beyond traditional processes

trust_orientation.value: contributors emphasize professional and integrity-based public administration, independent judiciaries and media, civil-society space, academic freedom, and freedom of expression

technology_orientation.value: AI-enabled democratic practices, algorithmic-bias safeguards, deliberative processes, multilevel governance, and peer exchange are identified as resilience instruments

observations.method: Council of Europe synthesis of consultation themes and emerging policy directions.
observations.uncertainty: The orientations are normative and strategic; they do not establish that institutions currently meet these standards or that any single instrument causes trust or resilience.
observations.subgroup: Citizens, public administrations, courts, media, schools, civil society, academics, technology providers, and local and national governments.
observations.counterinterpretation: New participation and digital tools can widen voice, but without access, privacy, moderation, and accountability they may reproduce exclusion or intensify manipulation.

denominator.unit: interconnected pillars in the Council of Europe's democratic-parameters framework

pillars.value: democratic participation; independent and effective democratic institutions; democratic governance and integrity; democratic freedoms, inclusion and civil society; democratic future

vital_areas.unit: vital areas of democratic life covered by the framework

future_focus.value: empowering young people and children, education for democracy, and sustainable and innovative democratic life

observations.method: Council of Europe translation of Reykjavik Principles into a structured reference framework for voluntary self-assessment and mutual learning.
observations.uncertainty: The Parameters are standards and assessment tools, not a comparative scorecard or evidence that member states have implemented every area.
observations.subgroup: Member states, democratic institutions, civil society, young people, children, political parties, courts, and local authorities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Common standards can support accountability and learning, but voluntary self-assessment may produce uneven reporting and cannot replace independent monitoring or remedy.

denominator.unit: Council of Europe strategic security framing

threat_pathways.value: foreign information manipulation, disinformation, war, social vulnerability, scapegoating, shrinking civic space, and technology moving faster than democratic safeguards

security_reframe.value: human rights, democracy, rule of law, social rights, health, education, and institutional trust are treated as foundations of democratic security rather than soft security

implementation_horizon.value: final Pact outcomes and commitments are expected in 2027 after consultation and targeted initiatives

observations.method: Council of Europe strategic synthesis connecting geopolitical rupture, social vulnerability, technology, institutional trust, rights, and democratic resilience.
observations.uncertainty: The framing identifies pathways and proposed responses but does not quantify threat prevalence, estimate causal effects, or establish implementation outcomes.
observations.subgroup: European populations, minority groups, people at risk of poverty or exclusion, displaced populations, institutions, media, schools, and civic organizations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Security framing can elevate social rights and trust, but it can also justify overbroad restrictions unless legality, proportionality, rights, and democratic accountability remain explicit.

related_sources.claim: Council of Europe report landing page and chapter structure for the New Democratic Pact for Europe.
Complementary Council of Europe human-rights and democratic-resilience work.

boundary: This record adds a European democratic-security and institutional-trust route linking war and geopolitical rupture, information manipulation, social rights, civic space, elections, inclusion, digital technology, AI, and democratic participation. It is a strategic report and consultation synthesis, not a representative public-opinion survey, democracy score, causal security model, or proof that proposed Pact actions have been implemented.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Council of Europe Secretary-General 2026 report PDF and official landing page were reviewed for consultation scale, emerging orientations, Reykjavik Parameters, democratic-security framing, and implementation horizon.
